attrs.text: **Filtered files and submodules** — local diffs bypass clean/process filters; Git's built-in newline, ident, and encoding conversions still apply. Materialized LFS files and other filtered files can appear changed even when ordinary Git considers them clean; pointer-only checkouts compare normally. The panel does not request LFS downloads. Filter overrides rely on Git 2.31 or newer; older Git can ignore them and run helpers under Session permissions. Drivers added between enumeration and diff are not covered by the overrides. Submodule commit changes remain visible; internal uncommitted changes are omitted.

attrs.text: **Review thread writes** — a write through one changes view shows in other open views of the change request at their next status, or after `reviewRefreshMs` for a resolve, which does not change the pull request's update time. GitHub keeps one pending review per user and pull request. A comment draft an earlier version kept in the browser can join the pending review only while its file and lines still match the shown diff; otherwise it can only be edited or deleted. A comment on chosen commits can only be added to the input. Minimized comments show like others, and avatars load from the code host's image server in the browser.

title: **Review page** — only the GitHub provider lists change requests and reads descriptions, so the lists hold GitHub hosts, each provider's configured hosts together; a GitLab merge request opened from a pasted link shows its status, changes, ...

attrs.text: **Review page** — only the GitHub provider lists change requests and reads descriptions, so the lists hold GitHub hosts, each provider's configured hosts together; a GitLab merge request opened from a pasted link shows its status, changes, and chat, with a read failure in place of its description. Choosing among hosts and accounts waits for a second provider that lists change requests. The changes tab shows no plugin lenses, annotations, toolbar, file-menu, or comment-form entries, whose extension points name a Session, and its quotes go to the chat's draft instead of the Session's input. The chat starts in the Workspace's shared blank Session, which New Session also shows, and does not check that the Workspace is a checkout of the repository; the change request to bind waits in Host memory until the first message, so a Host restart forgets it. Pending review comments last while the page shows their change request.

title: **Restoring** — restoring recreates the checkout from the branch, or from the commit the branch started from when the branch is gone; changes that were never committed are lost with the removed directory. The [worktree service](../worktree/...

attrs.text: **Restoring** — restoring recreates the checkout from the branch, or from the commit the branch started from when the branch is gone; changes that were never committed are lost with the removed directory. The [worktree service](../worktree/README.md#use-this-package) validates the recorded target and removes only its missing, unlocked registration. An existing or incomplete directory stays blocked; preserve its files and remove the directory before retrying, or continue in the source project.

title: **Linked-worktree projects** — the option is unavailable when the project is itself a linked worktree, unless the sandbox policy grants its Git directory: under workspace-write that directory lies outside the writable root, so neither the n...

attrs.text: **Linked-worktree projects** — the option is unavailable when the project is itself a linked worktree, unless the sandbox policy grants its Git directory: under workspace-write that directory lies outside the writable root, so neither the new branch nor later commits could be written. A grant registered while the panel shows takes effect at the next inspection. Windows processes ignore such grants, so there the option is offered and creation fails. Commits inside a created worktree need the grant too, as the [worktree service](../worktree/README.md#known-limitations-and-deferred-work) describes.

A review write costs one GraphQL query for the head check and one mutation, or two for a pending reply that starts the pending review.

title: **Limited shell recognition** — Only CLIs with a registered rule bind. Numeric selectors require a literal repository. Expansion, substitutions, multiline scripts, undeclared options, and aliases are excluded. Unqualified repositories in co...

attrs.text: **Limited shell recognition** — Only CLIs with a registered rule bind. Numeric selectors require a literal repository. Expansion, substitutions, multiline scripts, undeclared options, and aliases are excluded. Unqualified repositories in compound commands or PowerShell require an output URL or `track`; the live resolver cannot recover their original environment. Replay restores confirmed reference records and selectors that name their host without running a lookup; old unqualified calls without a recorded URL need another invocation or `track`. Branch selectors and `git push --porcelain` remain unsupported.

title: **Rule changes refold every Session** — a provider that adds a rule or raises its version invalidates every checkpointed `forgeChangeRequests` row: each Session refolds its whole log when next read, and until then the Session list shows no ...

attrs.text: **Rule changes refold every Session** — a provider that adds a rule or raises its version invalidates every checkpointed `forgeChangeRequests` row: each Session refolds its whole log when next read, and until then the Session list shows no cached bindings for it. A Session read during startup, before the providers register, folds without their commands, and a checkpoint written then folds again at the next start. Starting without a provider removes the bindings that only its commands made, such as those of `gh pr create` without forge-github; binding records stay. Re-registration emits no projection change, so an open Session's summary shows the refolded bindings once a later event changes its projection state; watchers and `changeRequests` see them at once.

On Git that meets the execution requirements, missing local objects cause creation to fail.

Git LFS pointers and encrypted blobs stay in their stored representation; hydration or decryption is a separate user-controlled operation.

title: **Execution requirements** — the subprocess provider must offer Git and Node in the same execution world as the filesystem provider. Git must honor `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH`, which Git 2.45 and the 2.39.4, 2.40.2, 2.41.1, 2.42.2, 2.43.4, and 2.44...

attrs.text: **Execution requirements** — the subprocess provider must offer Git and Node in the same execution world as the filesystem provider. Git must honor `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH`, which Git 2.45 and the 2.39.4, 2.40.2, 2.41.1, 2.42.2, 2.43.4, and 2.44.1 maintenance releases do; older releases ignore it and proceed instead of failing, so creation can fetch missing partial-clone objects from a promisor remote. The `git --no-lazy-fetch` option would reject these releases, but it exists only in Git 2.45 and later and also rejects the patched maintenance releases. The existing sandbox must permit all checkout and shared Git metadata writes.

title: **Commits inside a worktree** — the repository's Git directory lies outside a linked worktree, so under `workspace-write` a Session that works in one cannot run `git add` or `git commit`, or create another worktree from it, until the [sandb...

attrs.text: **Commits inside a worktree** — the repository's Git directory lies outside a linked worktree, so under `workspace-write` a Session that works in one cannot run `git add` or `git commit`, or create another worktree from it, until the [sandbox policy](../../sandbox/sandbox-policy/README.md#use-this-package) grants that directory through `additionalWritableRoots` or `registerWritableRoot`. This service registers no grant, and Windows processes ignore such grants.
